en: The Chapter on Similes, The Lion Section.
5. The Question of the Owl’s Limbs “Venerable Nāgasena, when you say that ‘two limbs of the owl should be adopted,’ which are those two limbs that should be adopted?
“Just as, Great King, the owl is at enmity with the crows; having gone to the flock of crows at night, it kills many of them.”
In the same way, Great King, the practitioner of yoga, the yogāvacara, should act in opposition to ignorance. Sitting alone in seclusion, he should crush ignorance and cut it off at the root.
This, Great King, is the first quality of the owl that should be adopted.
Furthermore, Great King, the owl is well-reclined in solitude.
In the same way, Great King, a yogi practicing yoga should be one who delights in seclusion and takes pleasure in seclusion.
This, Great King, is the second quality of the owl that should be adopted.
And this, Great King, was spoken by the Blessed One, the God above Gods, in the excellent Saṃyutta Nikāya:
“Here, monks, a bhikkhu delights in seclusion and rejoices in seclusion; he understands as it really is: ‘This is suffering’;
he understands as it really is: ‘This is the origin of suffering’; he understands as it really is: ‘This is the cessation of suffering’;
he understands as it really is: ‘This is the way leading to the cessation of suffering.’”
The fifth question: The Question of Ulūkaṅga.
